name: Halo-Goliath
description: Halo-Goliath fills half the sky of anything that comes close, a banded colossus wrapped in a debris ring three hundred thousand kilometers wide. The ring is fed by a neighboring asteroid belt the planet has been cannibalizing for eons, so its ice and iron shards glitter like a spilled jewel-box against the amber cloud decks. Storms the size of continents churn in the upper atmosphere, some older than any recorded civilization.

From inside the ring itself, the view is intimate and violent: shattered rock tumbling past viewport glass, the giant's shadow slicing the belt into sudden midnight, lightning crawling between cloud towers below. The thin haze of pulverized regolith makes everything sound muffled even through a hull. Pilots call flying the ring 'sewing the halo' and charge accordingly.

The mining platform Ferrous Crown went dark forty years ago mid-harvest, its crew logs ending without distress call, and it still rides a stable ring orbit with every airlock sealed from the inside. Rumors insist someone moved in afterward—sensors keep catching heat blooms near the derelict that vanish when approached. The belt prospectors who know refuse to say more.

Helium-3 skimmers can refuel entire fleets here if they survive the radiation belts and the debris, which makes Halo-Goliath the most valuable fuel stop in three sectors—and the most lawless. The navy patrols the approaches but never the ring, where a hidden dock carved into a forty-meter asteroid serves whoever pays. Every faction in the region wants the hideout's coordinates; the hideout's current tenants want to stay legends.
